_comment: Speed budgets. 'target' is the goal from the release plan; 'guard' is the
regression limit CI enforces today (measured baseline plus headroom).
A metric over its guard fails CI. Over target but within guard is reported
as tracked until the work that brings it in lands, then the guard drops to
the target. Never raise a guard to make CI pass: lower it when you improve
a metric, and explain any increase in the PR.
where: mac = macOS CI runner (release build, signed app); linux-webkit = CI WebKit.
Guards set 2026-10-11 from the first CI run, ~1.3-1.5x the measurement:
update_100kb 17.9, update_1mb 227.6, warm_open 1239, cold_start 5060,
write_to_update 423, web_first_apply_1mb 1351, web_update_20 197, long frames 417/600.
Revised 2026-10-11 after repeat runs showed run-to-run noise on shared runners:
warm_open 1239 and 1730 -> guard 2600; web_first_apply_1mb 1351 and 2096 -> 3000;
web_update_20 now includes the layout it causes: 225 and 459 ms in two runs -> guard 700;
scroll frame pacing in headless WebKit varied 417-528 long frames of 600 with no code
change, so scroll metrics are reported, not gated (guard null).
The macOS runner varies as much: update_100kb 17.9 and 26.6, update_1mb 227.6 and 355.7,
cold_start 5060 and 6462, write_to_update 423 and 466 with no parser change, so those
guards are ~1.5x the highest run: 40, 530, 9700, 700.
Since the open timings end at the first presented frame (not the synchronous apply), runs
measured warm_open 2587 and cold_start 8502: guards 3900 and 12800 (1.5x).
write_to_update measured to the painted frame: 936 ms (496 to the apply in the same
kind of run; the runner's display paces frames slowly) -> guard 1400.
Incremental parsing (M5): update_100kb 12.7 ms, update_1mb 66.1 ms on the macOS runner;
guards lowered to 20 and 100 (1.5x).
Word-level comparison (M6) runs inside the update for each edited block (word_diff_100kb
1.2-2.5 ms for the 20 edits). Eight macOS runs of the M6 branch measured update_100kb
12.1-25.9 ms and update_1mb 55.6-112.9 ms (the M5 runs: 11.0-16.9 and 59.2-91.2), with
no parser change between the fastest and slowest; a Linux release build measured the
same before and after the last M6 commits. Guards raised to 30 and 150 so runner noise
does not fail CI; targets unchanged.
3.2: update_100kb and update_1mb are measured on the fastest of 9 / 7 runs (runner
interference only adds time). Three macOS runs of the same commit: update_100kb 11.2,
11.7, 11.7 ms; update_1mb 59.0, 56.6, 51.9 ms. Guards lowered to 18 and 90 (1.5x the
highest); both now meet their targets.
3.4: update_1mb_minstr is the same update counted in instructions (millions) by valgrind
in the Linux core job (Packages/ReadoutCore/Tools/perf-instructions.sh), which runner noise
does not move. 3.3.0 measured 842 with Swift 6.1 on Linux; 3.4 (byte scans, parallel fragment
parsing) 395. Target: half of 3.3.0. Guard 1.3x the 3.4 measurement.
With those changes two macOS runs measured update_100kb 5.7 and 5.1 ms, update_1mb 25.4 and
23.4 ms (3.3.0: 12.0-12.7 and 64.6-78.6): guards lowered to 12 and 50 (about 2x the higher,
since parallel parsing on a shared runner may vary more); targets unchanged.
3.4 (web): web_update_20_blocks_1mb_ms now waits two frames after the scroll before the
update, so the scroll's own layout is no longer counted, and the update measures the blocks
it changed once after its ops instead of once per op (one layout instead of 20). Three CI
runs: 18, 21, 16 ms (3.3 on the old harness: 131-245 ms). Guard 700 -> 40: about 2x the
highest, since shared-runner runs of one commit have differed 2x (225 and 459 above).
web_first_apply_1mb_painted_ms (new): first apply until the frame showing it is painted;
three CI runs 3288, 2406, 1934 ms -> guard 4900 (1.5x the highest). web_first_apply_1mb_ms
measured 2361, 1610, 1266 in the same runs (unchanged code; 1017-2201 before): guard stays 3000.
3.5: warm_open_ms is the median of three opens of the same document in one smoke run (each
sample is printed as warm_open_samples_ms). One 3.4 run measured 4084 ms against 1670-2287 in
the others with no app change, its cold_start 8603 ms also the slowest: the runner, not the
code. The guard stays 3900; the median keeps one slow moment from deciding.
3.6: a guard below its target contradicts what the two mean (over target but within guard is
'tracked'; a run that meets the target must not fail). update_1mb's guard 50 was under its
target 60, and main failed at 51.7 ms with no parser change (3.4 measured 23.4-25.4): the
runner, as the 3.2 notes record (51.9-59.0 for one commit). Guard 75: 1.25x the target, about
1.45x the highest run. update_100kb's guard 12 was under its target 15 the same way: 18
(1.2x the target; measured 5.1-5.7). Every guard is now at least its target (CorePerfBudgetFile test).
3.6 (web): the first open of a large document reads no layout before its first frame, and
web_first_apply_1mb_ms is now the synchronous apply (perf.test no longer forces a layout
between the apply and the painted frame). Three CI runs of the same commit: 180, 180, 183 ms
(the old metric, apply plus a forced layout of every block: 1266-2361) -> guard 600, room for
the 2x shared-runner swings seen before. web_first_apply_1mb_painted_ms 1385, 1815, 1881
(3.4: 1934-3288) -> guard 2800 (1.5x the highest). web_update_20_blocks_1mb_ms 15, 14, 15
(3.4: 16-21) with no layout forced per patch beyond the update's own -> guard 30 (2x).
3.6 (core speed): blocks without a checkbox in their source skip the walk over their Markdown
tree for task items, lines are split on bytes (not Characters) for math protection and the
renderer, code-span path checks test bytes, and the session keeps the previous version's
block keys for blocks that did not change. update_1mb_minstr 405.3 on main (CI) -> 330.2
(Linux, Swift 6.1, as CI). Instruction counts repeat within about 2%, so the guard is 1.15x
the measurement: 380; the target (half of 3.3.0, 421) is above that, so it drops to 350.
New counts in the same job (Tools/perf-instructions.sh SCENARIO): append_1mb_minstr, one
paragraph appended to the 1 MB document (an agent writing on): 275.3 on main -> 243.9, guard
280, target 260. open_1mb_unique_minstr, the first open of 1 MB whose blocks are all distinct
(the corpus repeated with each repetition's prose marked, so nothing is shared): 3820 on main
append_patch_bytes_1mb: the JSON the page gets for that append (perf-probe bytes append).
Every patch carried the document's whole outline, task counts and title, which the page never
reads: 142,255 bytes on main (754,177 at 5 MB). Now the page gets RenderPatch.Page: 272 bytes,
one paragraph and the envelope. Guard 400: room for richer paragraph HTML, while anything
sized by the document fails it.
3.7 (web): web_first_highlight_warm_ms, the synchronous first apply of a small document with a
TypeScript block on screen, on a page warmed as the app's spare page is. Loading a grammar does
not compile its patterns, so this cost 170-220 ms on a warm open; the spare page's warm-up now
compiles each preloaded grammar's patterns and a sample, in slices, once it has sat unused for
5 s. Target 40, guard 80. web_hl_warm_longest_step_ms: its longest single step (one pattern:
what a window taking the page mid-warm-up could wait for), reported, not gated.
3.7: warm_open_to_applied_ms is Readout's own share of warm_open_ms: window request to the
page's first apply (the fastest of the same three opens), without the frame the system paints
it in. The 3.6 audit measured ~350 ms of a 1.7-2.6 s warm_open on the runner: target 150,
guard 550. ql_open_ms (Quick Look, preparePreviewOfFile to the page's first apply, from the
extension's log) is reported, not gated, until a few runs show its spread.
3.7: warm_open_to_applied_ms gates the fastest of the three opens, not their median. The median
swung 416-693 ms between runs of code that does not touch the open path (main b889273: samples
768/416/403; core PR head 2fd5300: 1274/451/693); runner stalls only add time, so the minimum
(403 and 451 there) is the stable reading. The minimum still moves with the runner: this PR's
own run of main's code measured 790/703/507 ms, so the fastest open of unchanged code ranged
403-507 ms. The 550 guard came from a single 358 ms reading; it is now 800 (about 1.5x the
highest fastest-open seen on unchanged code, the file's usual rule). Target stays 150.
3.7 (web): web_stream_append_5mb_ms is an agent streaming at the end of a ~5 MB document
(25,000 blocks) while the reader follows: the median apply plus the layout it causes over 40
patches (perf.test.mjs). The page no longer searches the whole document per patch and lays
it out once instead of up to three times; locally (2-core Linux, WebKit) the same scenario
measured 206-229 ms on main and 170-175 ms after (apply alone 138-156 -> 92-97). Most of what
is left is the engine's own layout and scroll of 25,000 blocks (raw append ~50 ms). Reported,
not gated, until CI runs show its spread.
3.7, later the same day: the same tree measured 475 ms (core PR head 64b2d9c, main merged in)
and 851 ms (main b405e72, its squash; identical files) as the fastest of three opens, and
main went red at 800. On the shared macOS runner this number swings ~2x with no code change,
so it can only catch gross regressions: guard 2000 (about 2.3x the worst reading of unchanged
code), like warm_open_ms. Target 150 unchanged; the samples stay in the log for comparison.
3.7 (core, P1+P2): an update that differs from the previous version in one run of lines is
spliced into it (IncrementalParser.splice: fragmenting and assembly resume at the change and
stop once back in step; the blocks before it and, when no heading changed, after it are kept),
and the session compares only the blocks after those it kept (Differ.diff(old:new:shared:))
and builds the baseline when it is read, not on every update. append_1mb_minstr: 248.4 on main
(CI) -> 15.0. About 10 of that is decoding the 1 MB file as UTF-8 (FileContent.decode), which
every update does. Such a step is too small for the process difference: the two runs
perf-instructions.sh subtracts differ by about +-5 Minstr with the load's threads (this PR's
first CI run read 26.4, local runs 14.4-19.0 for the same code), so append and tail now count
the step alone (callgrind --toggle-collect on measuredUpdate; it runs on one thread, which the
script checks), which repeats to within 0.01%. Counted that way main measures 244.0 (append) and
245.8 (tail). Guards 1.15x the CI readings, the file's usual rule (17.3 and 16.6: 17 each);
targets the readings rounded up (16 and 15).
tail_1mb_minstr: a few words added to the 1 MB document's last line (an agent streaming
mid-line; perf-probe tail): 245.8 on main -> 14.4. update_1mb_minstr (20 paragraphs edited
throughout: one changed run spanning most of the document) moves less, 346.2 -> 332.9; its
budget is unchanged.
3.8 (P5): cold_start_ms (spawn to the first painted frame) measured 6895, 7994 and 8534 ms on
the runner, but Readout's own share is under 1 s: about 2.5 s is launch and the first code-signing
assessment of a fresh ad-hoc bundle, ~2.2 s WebKit's first process start, ~1 s the runner's paint.
It is now reported, not gated, and split into phases (timings.json launch_phases_ms, from the
process start time sysctl gives). The first CI run of this split (PR #70, 0dbd77d), ms since process
start: didFinishLaunching 2371, window init 3757, didLoad 5028, page ready 7600, apply 8007, paint 9430.
cold_page_ready_ms (didFinishLaunching, where the spare page is made, to its ready): 5228.6 there, nearly
all of it WebKit's first WebContent process start, which Readout does not control: reported, not gated.
Gated, what Readout owns: cold_apply_ms, the later of page ready and the document read (didLoad) to the
page's first apply (407.2; target 150 from the audit, guard 600, 1.47x), and cold_window_to_load_ms,
window init to didLoad: reading, parsing, the reading state and the git baseline, no WebKit (1271; guard
1900, 1.5x). Lower both once a few runs show their spread.
ql_page_ready_ms (P9): Quick Look's web view created, before the parse, to its page's ready,
from the extension's log. Reported, not gated, like ql_open_ms.
3.8 (P4): mid_1mb_minstr (new), a sentence added to a paragraph in the middle of a 1 MB document
of the corpus documents that define no footnotes, between two other paragraphs (perf-probe mid):
3.7 parsed it in full whenever a `[^` or `]:` came after the change (04-rou3's `([^x]*)`), 195.2;
spliced through such text when no footnotes are defined, 25.9 (Linux, Swift 6.1, as CI): about
10 decoding the file, 11 the session copying the blocks after the change, 3.5 the splice. Guard
1.15x (30), target the reading rounded up (26). The deep-nesting guard (B1, NestingCap) scans
every parsed fragment, and definitions are looked for across lines (a label on two): update_1mb
3.8 (web): three new metrics, reported (guard null) until CI runs show their spread.
web_edit_above_5mb_ms: an agent's edit 50 blocks above the reader in the 5 MB document, the
apply plus the layout it causes (median of six). The page rewrote the block's
contain-intrinsic-size and read offsetParent per block, and either makes WebKit lay out every
skipped block again: 2.3-4.5 s per edit locally before, 45-140 ms after. web_toc_jump_5mb_ms:
an outline jump from the top to a heading 30/55/80% down, until the frame showing it is
painted (median); it no longer forces content-visibility on 40 blocks. web_scroll_up_jump_px:
40 steps of 400 px up from the end of the 1 MB document, one per frame, the text under the
middle of the window moving beyond the scroll, summed (blocks laid out a frame after they
came into view grow upward now): 4449 px locally before, 941-1199 after.
Gated from four CI runs of PR #73 (bd7cf65 reruns, 447634f, 443c267; the 3 metrics, same code
path): web_edit_above_5mb_ms 50, 42, 30, 45 -> target 50, guard 75 (1.5x the highest; main's
path measured 1.5-4 s locally, so any return of the whole-page relayout fails it).
web_toc_jump_5mb_ms 368, 277, 205, 269 -> target 300, guard 550 (1.5x the highest: most of it
is WebKit laying out the landing frame, which swings with the runner). web_scroll_up_jump_px
340 in every run (frame-timed but it repeated exactly; 2956 on the first head, before the P6
fallback) -> target 340, guard 400 (1.18x: a deterministic count, as the instruction counts).
3.8 release review: mid_1mb_minstr measured 28.8 on CI at the release head (the P4 reading,
25.9, was taken before the copy lane's link definitions and the deep-nesting guard merged with
it): target 29 (the reading rounded up), guard 33 (1.15x). cold_start_ms gets back a loose
guard, 12800 (the 3.7 one, 1.5x-1.9x the 6895-8534 readings above): a tripwire for a launch
that crashes or hangs, not a speed budget; cold_apply_ms and cold_window_to_load_ms stay the
gated share Readout owns.
3.9 (speed): the grammars are converted to ES2018 regexes at build time (oniguruma-to-es, Shiki's
options) and the engine converts the rest for ES2018; @shikijs/langs-precompiled is gone. WebKit
compiled the v-flag patterns 200-500x slower: TypeScript's grammar 5.4-7.1 s against 0.9 s locally.
web_first_highlight_cold_ts_ms (new): a page not warmed (the first window at launch, a burst of
background tabs), set up as a window does, a TypeScript block applied at once, until it is
highlighted. Reported, not gated, until CI runs show its spread (locally 3.9-5.5 s before, ~1.1 s after).
The app preloads and warms only shellscript, json and typescript (12 before), and only a page still
the spare warms up. web_hl_warm_longest_step_ms is dropped: with three grammars the warm-up is a
quarter of the work, and its longest step is TypeScript's largest pattern, which ES2018 cut. web_tab_private_mb
(new): the warmed page's WebContent private memory (Linux smaps) with a small plan in it, 153 MB
locally with 12 grammars, 119 with 3.
web_scroll_long_frames (and the p95/max frame gaps beside it in perf-web.json) are dropped: 482-545 of
600 frames were 'long' in every run because each frame jumps ~703 px onto blocks not laid out yet;
noise, not what a reader feels. web_scroll_up_jump_px (gated) covers scrolling.
cold_window_to_load_ms is reported, not gated: in every run page_ready lands after did_load, so it is
not on the cold critical path (six main runs 624-1748 ms). The spare page is now made in
willFinishLaunching (launch phases will_finish_launching, spare_created, open_requested are new);
cold_page_ready_ms counts from there. cold_dfl_to_window_ms (new): didFinishLaunching to the first
window, all on the main thread before the window exists (1.0-2.0 s in six main runs), reported until
a few CI runs of this change are in, then gated at 1.5x the highest.
warm_open_to_applied_ms: guard 2000 -> 1000. Six main runs measured 348-632 ms (fastest of three
opens); 1000 is 1.6x the highest, and still above the target 150.
ql_second_open_ms (new, reported): a second qlmanage -p right after the first; the extension keeps
one spare page for the next preview.
3.9 (find): web_find_open_1mb_ms, the find bar's first search in the 1 MB document (find.js
reads every block's text without layout, counts, selects a match on screen; median of three).
3.8 laid out the whole document as the find bar opened (findMode: 2.9-7.0 s locally, ~1 s on
CI) and again as it closed. CI: 46 ms on the first run -> target 50, guard 100.
web_find_refresh_1mb_ms (new, reported): with a search on, an agent's one-block edit of the 1 MB
document, the page searching again for the count and the marks (median of three).
3.9 (cold apply, owner decision 2026-10-21): the first WebKit launch on a fresh VM is not what users
pay, so cold_apply_ms is now measured on the job's second app launch (tools/smoke-run.py launches
Readout once on a copy of the document, lets it paint and quit, then makes the measured launch: a new
process, no page kept). Same name, same definition, same budget (target 150, guard 600). Instrumented
CI runs found the first launch's page doing the same work as any later one, 2-3x slower: its first
setAppearance 50-75 ms (30-45 later), the first apply's block work 50-150 (23-35) and the layout it
reads 150-400 (70-110); cold_apply_ms 215-639 on the first launch, 140-206 on later ones of the same
runner. No grammar loads or compiles before the first apply, and the apply is sent 2-18 ms after the
page is ready. Spotlight off or a quiet machine did not change it. The first launch's value stays
visible as cold_apply_first_boot_ms (reported), with the page's split of the measured launch:
cold_page_setappearance_ms, cold_page_blocks_ms, cold_page_layout_ms (reported; *_first_boot_ms for
the first launch). cold_start_ms, launch_phases_ms, cold_page_ready_ms, cold_dfl_to_window_ms and
cold_window_to_load_ms stay the first launch's, as before. warm_open_ms, warm_open_to_applied_ms and
write_to_update_ms are measured in the second launch's process now (all after its first document).
3.9 (release review): web_find_one_letter_5mb_ms (new), Return in a find for "e" at the top of the 5 MB
document (about 300,000 matches): the two frames after the call, median of three. Before: 7.3 s locally
(WebKit checking every content-visibility block against the new selection); after 0.4 s locally,
most of it the landing's own layout (a word that matches 18,000 times costs about the same).
The first CI run measured 1026 ms (web_toc_jump_5mb_ms 242 in the same run); the samples are printed
as web_find_one_letter_5mb_samples_ms ([the call, the first frame, both frames]). Reported until
more CI runs of it are in.
3.9.1 (launch): 3.9.0 made the spare page in willFinishLaunching (F5); WebKit's start there held up
the rest of the launch (willFinishLaunching to didFinishLaunching 407 ms in later launches, 3.8.0 104;
2.0 s in a VM's first launch, 3.8.0 0.75 s) and the first window. A/B on the macOS runner under one
harness (3.8.0, 3.9.0 and the fix built alike; one variant per VM, a first launch and four later ones
each): spawn to the first window on screen, median, later launches 967 / 1076 / 958 ms (n=48 each), first
launches 3295 / 3679 / 3326 (n=12). The first window now makes its own page and the spare follows its
first paint. cold_window_visible_ms (new): spawn to the first window on screen (its occlusion state
visible), the measured (second) launch's; gated at 2700, 1.5x the highest of 3.8.0 and the fix in those
runs (1786); cold_window_visible_first_boot_ms, the job's first launch, reported. cold_start_second_ms
(spawn to the measured launch's first document painted, end to end) is gated at 6700, 1.5x the highest
of eight 3.9 main runs (1625-4442). cold_page_ready_ms now counts from the first window (which makes the
page), and cold_window_to_load_ms includes that page's making: both stay reported.
3.9.1 (find marks): web_find_next_1mb_frame_ms (new), Return with a search for "the" on in the 1 MB document,
until the frame showing the match is painted (median of seven; the next frame, which selects the match,
is printed in web_find_next_1mb_frame_samples_ms as [the call, to that frame, the next frame]).
web_find_refresh_1mb_frame_ms (new): an agent's one-block edit while finding, the longest frame in the
half second after it (the apply's frame and the refresh's, 100 ms later; median of five). 3.9.0 set both
highlights again on every Return and every edit, and held live ranges, which WebKit repaints on any
change of the page. Same harness, locally (Linux WebKit, noisy shared machine), 3.8.0 (59acabc,
window.find with findMode on) / 3.9.0 / this change: Next 29-30 / 51-74 / 47-71 ms; edit frame 36-41 /
59-137 / 20-33 ms; one-letter Return at 5 MB (web_find_one_letter_5mb_ms's measure) 216-220 (after
46 s of findMode) / 456-613 / 204-330 ms. First CI run of this change: Next 34 (samples 27-46), edit
frame 18 (17-23), one letter at 5 MB 1025 (1021-1034; 3.9.0 main 1038 and 1042, its first frame
61-75 now against 114-153). Guards about 1.5x the highest sample: next target 40 guard 70; refresh frame
target 25 guard 40; web_find_one_letter_5mb_ms guard 1500 (target 200 unchanged: on CI almost all of
it is the second frame after the landing, not the marks). The selection frame after Next (~95 ms on CI,
WebKit checking every content-visibility block against a new selection) is reported, not gated: it is
SELECTABLE's cost, not the marks'.
web_find_refresh_1mb_frame_ms guard 45 (3.9.1, after the chunks): the frame varies with the runner type more
than with the build. 3.8.0 has no in-page find, so 3.9.0 (c4b65f0) is the baseline, interleaved with 9331bbe
on one runner: on a slower one (experiment run 39878822650, 8 runs) medians 34-36 ms against 39-44, on a
faster one (39882235131, 5 runs) 29-31 against 26-28. The edit's own frame is 1-3 ms longer here on a fast
runner, up to 5-8 on a slow one; 3.9.0's later frame repainting the marks (40-70 ms) is gone. Guard: 3.9.0's
worst same-runner median, 36, x1.25 (x1.15 = 42 is under this build's worst on the slow runner type, 44).
3.9.1 (scrolling, chunks): the restored scroll measures (web/test/scrollperf.mjs) scroll a 500 KB agent
document with few code blocks (static, and with every eighth block changed and unread), the 1 MB and the
5 MB documents down through parts not seen yet, three ways (2400 px/s, flings, the browser's own wheel
events). Unlike the 3.8 pass (703 px jumps a frame, dropped in 3.9) they scroll as a reader does. Measured
with the same code on the Linux CI runner for 3.8.0 (59acabc, two runs) and with this change (PR #89):
6287/6432 -> 87, 22/25 -> 9-19 (CI; guard 22, 3.8.0's lowest). Blank rows over skipped content, summed over every frame: 3.8.0
2778-3468 px (500 KB), 0 now: web_scroll_blank_px is gated at 0. Guards: at most 3.8.0's value and about
2x ours (p95 a frame more, 34; frame gaps are paced at 16.7 ms); targets: ours. web_scroll_own_longest_ms,
the page's own longest callback while scrolling (code highlighting at 5 MB, one block at a time): 3.8.0
2848-2866, now 56-79 -> guard 150. Interactions (frames to the painted one): a selection change 1 MB
at 5 MB 44-54 (3.9.0 100732; 3.8.0 had WebKit's find) -> guard 100; Return until the match shows selected
at 1 MB (web_find_next_1mb_selected_ms) 25 (3.8.0 ~30 + ~20 for the selection) -> guard 50; three blocks
inserted in the middle of 5 MB and removed 640 -> 13-17 (40); an agent writing a patch every 100 ms at the
end of 5 MB, the reader following: frame p95 28/31 -> 27/31 (guard 34: two frames; 3.8.0 the same), long
frames 1 -> 0 (2). Lowered with them: web_toc_jump_5mb_ms 67-87 (3.8.0 323-372) -> guard 550 -> 200;
web_find_one_letter_5mb_ms 17-50 -> guard 1500 -> 200.
Re-measured with the final blank measure (it walks blocks and skipped chunks from the top of the
viewport; Codex: starting from a block it could not see a skipped chunk), two runs each on the Linux
runner, 3.8.0 / 3.9.0 / this change: blank px 500 KB 2964-2993 / 2822-3220 / 0, with marks 2703-2832 /
3.9.1: on a warmed page (the spare page a window opens on) 3.9.0 painted Python, Go, Swift, Rust, YAML
and diff plain and coloured them 54-182 ms later (3.8.0 coloured them in the first paint): 3.9 preloaded
three grammars instead of twelve. The spare page now also loads and compiles Python, Rust, YAML and diff
(Linux, warmed tab with a small plan, four runs each: 119-123 MB with three, 124-128 with seven: +4 MB;
Go would add ~7 more, Swift ~7 more, all twelve ~36), and the app sends the languages a document's fences
name as soon as it has read the file (readout.prepare), so the page loads and compiles them while the
document parses. web_warm_first_paint_plain_blocks (new): code blocks on screen not coloured inside the
synchronous apply of a document with a Python and a YAML block on the warmed page: guard 0 (3.9.0: 2).
web_first_highlight_warm_py_yaml_ms (new): that apply, 13 ms locally; the same target and guard as
web_first_highlight_warm_ms. web_tab_private_mb gets a guard: 3.9.0 measured 182-189 MB in most CI runs
and 210-214 in two (the runner), plus the 4 MB measured for the four grammars and 4 MB for the spread
within one mode: 222 (3.8.0's twelve preloaded grammars measured ~36 MB more than 3.9.0).

preloaded, so every language 3.8.0 coloured in a warm open's first paint is coloured there again, no
